issue_families.name: Password reset links invalidated or rejected
issue_families.summary: Single-use reset tokens are consumed or broken before the user redeems them (mail link scanners, superseded requests, redirects or line-wrapping that strip the token); users see 'already used', 'expired' or 'invalid token'.
issue_families.boundary_note: Credential recovery is part of signing in, so auth; it is not export or alerts even though an email carries the link.

issue_families.name: Password reset email not delivered or suppressed
issue_families.summary: Reset emails that are deferred, misrouted, suppressed by design for SSO-enforced accounts, rate-limited or never generated because of a template fault.
issue_families.boundary_note: Password-reset emails stay auth by policy; scheduled report emails are export and metric notifications are alerts.

issue_families.name: SAML assertion, attribute and endpoint mapping
issue_families.summary: Mismatched entity IDs, ACS URLs, NameID formats, clock skew or assertion parsing faults cause SSO errors or unmatched users.
issue_families.boundary_note: The failure happens at sign-in before any role is evaluated (not perm) and no network path is blocked (not connectivity).

issue_families.name: SSO signing certificate rotation and mix-ups
issue_families.summary: Identity provider or service provider signing certificates are rotated, renewed or uploaded wrongly, so assertion or request signatures fail and every SSO user is affected at once.
issue_families.boundary_note: These certificates sign SSO messages; they are sign-in credentials, not TLS/network certificates, so auth rather than connectivity.

issue_families.name: OIDC client configuration
issue_families.summary: Expired client secrets, unregistered redirect URIs, missing scopes or oversized tokens break OpenID Connect sign-in.
issue_families.boundary_note: This is people signing in through OIDC, not an integration calling the public API, so auth rather than api.

issue_families.name: Authenticator (TOTP) code verification
issue_families.summary: One-time codes are rejected because of device clock drift, stale enrollment secrets after device migration, input formatting or expired enrollment QR codes.
issue_families.boundary_note: Second-factor verification during login is auth.

issue_families.name: Two-factor enforcement and recovery
issue_families.summary: Problems rolling out mandatory 2FA, recovery codes, trusted-device cookies and owner resets of a lost second factor.
issue_families.boundary_note: Concerns sign-in requirements and recovery rather than what a role may access (perm).

issue_families.name: Account lockouts from stale or automated credentials
issue_families.summary: Lockout policy tripped by scripts, cached add-in passwords or kiosk autofill, lockouts extended by repeated attempts, or lockouts that actually originate at the identity provider.
issue_families.boundary_note: Lockout is a sign-in control; it is not offboarding or role management (perm).

issue_families.name: Session lifetime and multi-workspace sessions
issue_families.summary: Sessions ending earlier than users expect due to absolute versus idle limits, workspace switching, client clock errors, persistent-session policy or unattended screens.
issue_families.boundary_note: Session validity is auth; slow pages are perf and wrongly drawn dashboards are render.

issue_families.name: Browser cookie handling and login loops
issue_families.summary: Login loops or silent failures from third-party cookie blocking in embedded views, cookie name collisions on custom domains, blocked browser storage or managed cookie policies.
issue_families.boundary_note: The browser drops or never stores the session; the dashboard itself renders fine once signed in (not render) and no proxy or firewall is involved (not connectivity).

issue_families.name: Invitation acceptance and account activation
issue_families.summary: Invitation and activation links that expire, are consumed early, attach to the wrong identity or fail because of malformed addresses.
issue_families.boundary_note: Creating a user's sign-in identity is auth; what they can see once activated is perm.

issue_families.name: Sign-in identity matching
issue_families.summary: Users reach a new, empty or no account because their email, alias, letter case or domain differs from the stored login identity.
issue_families.boundary_note: Users may see empty workspaces, but the cause is which identity they signed in as, not role assignment, so auth rather than perm.

issue_families.name: Personal access tokens for user tools
issue_families.summary: Personal tokens used by the spreadsheet add-in or command-line tool are rejected after password changes, expiry, workspace scoping or blocked sign-in pop-ups.
issue_families.boundary_note: These tokens authenticate an individual user, so auth; keys used by system integrations against the public API are api.

issue_families.name: Mobile app sign-in
issue_families.summary: Biometric unlock, SSO hand-back to the app, cached workspace lookups, token persistence and sign-out on shared devices in the mobile app.
issue_families.boundary_note: Sign-in and session behaviour in the mobile app are auth; mobile chart layout would be render.

issue_families.name: Password policy and forced password changes
issue_families.summary: Complexity rules, breach screening, expiry loops, Unicode normalization and policy changes that reject passwords or trap users in change prompts.
issue_families.boundary_note: Credential rules are auth, distinct from general workspace defaults (workspace_admin).

related_groups.shared_root_cause: The customer's inbound email security scanner follows links in incoming mail and redeems the single-use password reset token before the user clicks it.
The customer's identity provider rotated its SAML signing certificate while the workspace SSO settings still trusted the old certificate.
The user's device clock drifted outside the TOTP validity window, so generated codes were rejected.
An unattended process (scheduled script, old add-in or kiosk browser autofill) keeps retrying an outdated password and trips the lockout policy.
Browsers block cookies set inside a cross-site iframe, so dashboards embedded in a customer portal cannot keep a session and loop back to the sign-in form.
The user's primary email changed in the identity provider, so SSO matching by email no longer finds the existing account.
Resetting or changing a password revokes all of the user's personal access tokens by design, breaking tools that still hold the old token.
The OIDC client secret in the customer's identity provider app registration expired, so the token exchange is rejected.
One session cookie was shared across workspaces, so signing in to a second workspace replaced the first workspace's session.

tickets.subject: Password reset link reports 'already used' on first click
tickets.description: Customer reports that password reset links open to 'This link has already been used' even when clicked within a minute of the email arriving. Several colleagues at the same company see the same message.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's inbound email security gateway opens every link in incoming mail to scan it, which redeemed the single-use reset token before the user clicked. As a workaround the user entered the six-digit reset code from the same email, which a link scanner cannot consume; a permanent change so that opening the link no longer redeems the token is tracked for a later release. Confirmed the user signed in with the new password.

tickets.subject: Reset emails work for personal mailbox but not company address
tickets.description: The customer's admin says head-office staff get 'Link expired or invalid' whenever they open a password reset email at their work address. A test account using a personal mailbox resets without any trouble.
tickets.resolution_notes: Audit logs showed each reset token redeemed from a scanning service a few seconds after delivery; the customer's mail filter pre-opens links only in messages to corporate mailboxes. Walked the affected staff through entering the reset code from the email instead of following the link, and attached the case to the scheduled change that will stop link opens from redeeming tokens. All four staff members confirmed they could sign in.

tickets.subject: Store managers' reset tokens redeemed seconds after delivery
tickets.description: Store managers at a pharmacy chain click the reset link and land on an error page. Agent review of the audit log showed each token had been redeemed from 198.51.100.23 within five seconds of the email being sent, long before anyone clicked.
tickets.resolution_notes: The address belonged to the link-protection service in the customer's mail platform, which fetches every URL in inbound mail. This release changed reset links to open a confirmation page that redeems the token only when the user presses 'Set new password', so automated fetches no longer invalidate it. Sent fresh reset emails after the update and confirmed three store managers completed the reset on the first attempt.

tickets.subject: Reset link rejected after requesting several resets
tickets.description: A user clicked 'Forgot password' four times because the first email seemed slow, then opened the first email and got 'This reset link is no longer valid'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each new reset request invalidates every earlier link for the account, so only the most recent email could work; the first email had simply arrived late. The user opened the newest email and reset successfully, and we updated the email wording to state that only the latest link is valid.

tickets.classification_rationale: Triggered by a workspace rename (workspace_admin), but the broken flow is credential recovery, so it is auth.
tickets.subject: Reset link opens the sign-in page instead of the reset form
tickets.description: After the customer renamed their workspace, users clicking password reset links are dropped on the normal sign-in page with no reset form and no error.
tickets.resolution_notes: Reset emails still used the workspace's previous subdomain, and the redirect from the old subdomain to the new one discarded the query string carrying the reset token. Fixed the redirect to preserve query parameters and changed reset emails to use the current subdomain. A fresh reset link opened the reset form and the user set a new password.

tickets.subject: 'Invalid reset token' when link is copied from plain-text email
tickets.description: User reads mail in a plain-text client and copies the reset URL into the browser; the page says the token is invalid. The link in the same email works when tapped on their phone.
tickets.resolution_notes: The plain-text version of the email wrapped the long reset URL onto two lines, so the user only copied the first part of the token. Shortened reset URLs so they fit on one line in plain-text mail and advised copying the full link in the meantime. The user's next reset link worked from the desktop client.

tickets.subject: No reset email for user on SSO-enforced workspace
tickets.description: A merchandising analyst tried 'Forgot password' and was told an email was on its way, but nothing came. Their workspace requires single sign-on for everyone.
tickets.resolution_notes: Password reset is intentionally disabled for accounts in workspaces that enforce SSO, but the reset page showed the same generic 'check your email' message to everyone. Directed the analyst to their company identity provider's self-service reset and changed the page to tell SSO-enforced users to use their company login. The analyst signed in via SSO the same day.

tickets.classification_rationale: Involves a DNS record, but the impact is delayed password-reset emails, which stay auth by category policy.
tickets.subject: Reset emails deferred 40+ minutes for one customer domain
tickets.description: Customer's admin reports that reset emails to anyone at their company arrive 40 to 70 minutes after the request. Messages to other domains arrive normally.
tickets.resolution_notes: A DKIM key rotation on our transactional mail domain left the published DNS record with a truncated key, so the customer's strict mail server treated our messages as failing sender authentication and deferred them. Corrected the DKIM record and released the queued messages. A test reset email to the customer's domain arrived in under a minute with DKIM passing.

tickets.subject: Reset emails routed to a moderated distribution list
tickets.description: A regional manager never sees their reset email. The customer's admin later found the messages waiting in the moderation queue of a team distribution list.
tickets.resolution_notes: The manager's login email was a team alias (regional-ops@retail.example.com) assigned during an early bulk import, so reset emails went to a moderated list. After the admin verified the manager's identity, we changed the login email to their individual mailbox. The next reset email arrived directly and the manager signed in.

tickets.classification_rationale: Language is a workspace preference, but the failure is a password-reset email not being sent, which is auth.
tickets.subject: German-language users receive no password reset email
tickets.description: Only users whose interface language is German never get password reset emails, according to the customer. English and French users at the same company are unaffected.
tickets.resolution_notes: A template refresh omitted the German variant of the reset email, and the send job failed for those users instead of falling back. Restored the German template and added an English fallback whenever a localized template is missing. A German-language user received the reset email within a minute and completed the reset.

tickets.subject: Repeated reset requests appear to do nothing
tickets.description: A store manager clicked 'Forgot password' six times in ten minutes and says no emails came at all, although the page showed the normal confirmation every time.
tickets.resolution_notes: The five emails that were sent had been filed into an archive folder by a mailbox rule, and the sixth request was silently dropped by the five-per-hour limit. With the customer's admin we found the emails through message tracking; the manager used the newest one, since each request invalidates the previous link, and signed in. The reset page now tells users when the hourly request limit has been reached.

tickets.subject: SSO error: audience restriction does not match
tickets.description: Every SSO attempt fails with 'AudienceRestriction mismatch' right after the customer's admin rebuilt the SAML app in their identity provider.
tickets.resolution_notes: The rebuilt app sent the entity ID with a trailing slash, while the workspace expects the exact value shown on its SSO settings page. The admin corrected the audience value in the identity provider app. Test sign-ins by the admin and two pilot users succeeded.

tickets.subject: SSO users get 'We couldn't match your account'
tickets.description: After the customer replaced their SAML app, all users authenticate at the identity provider and then see 'We couldn't match your account to a user in this workspace'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The new app sent a persistent opaque NameID instead of the user's email address, so no existing user matched. Walked the admin through setting the NameID format to email address in the customer's Okta tenant. Every user the admin tested was matched to their existing account.

tickets.classification_rationale: Started with a workspace subdomain change, but what failed is the SSO sign-in endpoint, so auth rather than workspace_admin.
tickets.subject: SAML response lands on 404 after subdomain change
tickets.description: Users completing SSO are sent to a 'Page not found' error. The admin moved the workspace to a custom subdomain the day before.
tickets.resolution_notes: The identity provider was still posting assertions to the assertion consumer service URL on the old subdomain, which no longer routes to the workspace. Gave the admin the new ACS URL from the SSO settings page and they updated the IdP app. SSO sign-in worked for all users from the next attempt.

tickets.subject: Intermittent 'assertion not yet valid' errors
tickets.description: Roughly a third of SSO sign-ins fail with 'Assertion is not yet valid'; they succeed if the user waits a few minutes and tries again.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's on-premises identity provider server clock was running about four minutes fast, so assertion validity windows started in the future. The customer resynchronized the server with their time source and enabled automatic time sync. No further validity errors appeared over the following two days of sign-ins.

tickets.subject: SSO fails for users with an apostrophe in their surname
tickets.description: Two users at an apparel retailer cannot sign in via SSO and see a generic 'Sign-in failed' page while everyone else signs in normally. Both have an apostrophe in their last name.
tickets.resolution_notes: Our SAML parser rejected attribute values containing an escaped apostrophe entity and failed the whole assertion. Fixed the parser to decode standard XML entities and added test cases for punctuation in names. Both users signed in after the fix was deployed.

tickets.classification_rationale: A certificate is involved, but it signs SSO assertions rather than securing a network connection, so auth rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: All SSO users fail with signature validation error
tickets.description: On Monday morning every user at the customer gets 'Signature validation failed' when signing in through SSO. It worked on Friday.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's identity provider rotated its SAML signing certificate over the weekend, and the workspace SSO settings still held the old certificate. The admin downloaded the new IdP metadata and uploaded it on the SSO settings page. SSO sign-in succeeded for the admin and a sample of users immediately afterwards.

tickets.classification_rationale: The failing certificate is the SSO signing credential, not a TLS certificate, so auth rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: Company-wide SSO outage with error SAML-SIG-002
tickets.description: Nobody at the customer can sign in through their identity provider; the error page shows reference SAML-SIG-002. The break-glass admin account with a local password still works.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's identity team replaced the IdP signing certificate during scheduled maintenance, so the fingerprint stored in the workspace no longer matched incoming assertions. The break-glass admin pasted the new certificate into the SSO settings, and we recommended pointing the workspace at the IdP metadata URL so future changes are picked up. Sign-ins resumed within minutes for all users.

tickets.subject: SSO breaks every time the IdP rotates its certificate
tickets.description: Customer's admin wants a lasting solution: SSO has broken twice this year when their identity provider's signing certificate rolled over, and each time they had to upload the new certificate by hand.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace used a static certificate upload, so each rotation broke signature validation until someone replaced it. Switched the workspace to read the IdP metadata URL nightly, which picks up new and overlapping certificates automatically and replaces the manual-upload workaround. During the customer's next planned rotation in their test tenant, the new certificate was picked up overnight and sign-ins continued without interruption.

tickets.subject: Signature validation fails during first SSO setup
tickets.description: A customer configuring SSO for the first time gets 'Signature validation failed' on every test sign-in, even though the certificate was copied from the identity provider minutes earlier.
tickets.resolution_notes: The admin had uploaded the IdP's encryption certificate rather than its signing certificate, so signatures could never verify. Pointed them to the signing certificate in the IdP metadata and they replaced it on the SSO settings page. Test sign-ins succeeded and SSO was switched on for the workspace.

tickets.classification_rationale: A certificate renewal is involved, but it is the credential used to sign SSO requests, so auth rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: IdP rejects sign-in requests after our certificate renewal
tickets.description: SSO stopped for a customer whose identity provider requires signed authentication requests. Users see an error from their own IdP, 'Request signature invalid', before they ever reach a login form.
tickets.resolution_notes: We had renewed the service-provider certificate used to sign authentication requests, and the customer's IdP still trusted only the old one. The customer imported our updated service-provider metadata, and admins now receive an email 30 days before such renewals. Sign-ins worked as soon as the import completed.

tickets.subject: 'Continue with SSO' fails with invalid_client
tickets.description: Customer using OpenID Connect sign-in reports that every attempt now ends on an error page reading 'invalid_client'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The client secret in the customer's identity provider app registration had reached its 12-month expiry, so the token exchange was rejected. The admin generated a new secret and entered it in the workspace SSO settings. Sign-in worked for all users immediately.

tickets.subject: OIDC sign-in returns 401 though nothing was changed
tickets.description: Since this morning the SSO button sends people back to the login page with 'Identity provider rejected the request (401)'. The customer insists nobody touched the configuration.
tickets.resolution_notes: Their IdP app registration enforces a 180-day secret lifetime, and the secret had lapsed overnight, so our token request failed authentication. The admin issued a new secret and updated the workspace; the SSO settings page now lets admins record the secret's expiry date and shows a banner 14 days ahead. Users signed in successfully within ten minutes.

tickets.subject: redirect_uri mismatch for new regional workspace
tickets.description: The customer created a second workspace hosted in our EU region. OIDC sign-in there fails at the identity provider with 'redirect_uri does not match a registered value'; the original workspace is fine.
tickets.resolution_notes: Only the callback URL for the original region was registered in the customer's IdP app. The admin added the EU workspace's callback URL shown on its SSO settings page. Sign-in to the EU workspace succeeded for the test users.

tickets.subject: OIDC sign-in bounces back to login with no message
tickets.description: After authenticating at their identity provider, users are returned to our login page with no error. It began after the admin edited the SSO settings to add a group claim.
tickets.resolution_notes: While editing, the admin had accidentally removed 'email' from the requested scopes, so the ID token carried no email address and the sign-in was discarded. Restored the email scope and added validation that blocks saving an OIDC configuration without it. Users signed in normally afterwards.

tickets.classification_rationale: Directory groups are involved, but the failure occurs during sign-in before any permission check, so auth rather than perm.
tickets.subject: HTTP 431 after SSO for users in many groups
tickets.description: Some users see 'Request header fields too large (431)' immediately after OIDC sign-in. All of them belong to well over a hundred directory groups; users with few groups are fine.
tickets.resolution_notes: The ID token listed every group membership, and keeping it in the session cookie pushed request headers past the server limit. The customer filtered the groups claim to the groups assigned to our app, and we moved token storage server-side so cookie size no longer depends on the claim. Affected users signed in without errors.

tickets.subject: Authenticator codes rejected every time
tickets.description: User says every six-digit code from their authenticator app is refused with 'Incorrect code', even when typed the moment it appears.
tickets.resolution_notes: Automatic time was switched off on the user's phone and its clock had fallen about three minutes behind, so codes were generated for the wrong time window. The user re-enabled network time on the phone. The next code was accepted.

tickets.subject: 2FA codes only work occasionally since returning from travel
tickets.description: A regional manager says their codes work 'maybe one time in five' since they came back from a trip abroad. They have not changed phones or reinstalled anything.
tickets.resolution_notes: During the trip the manager had set the phone's date and time manually, which left the clock roughly 50 seconds out after returning, so most codes fell just outside the accepted window. Switching the phone back to automatic date and time removed the offset. Five consecutive sign-ins with codes then succeeded.

tickets.subject: Codes rejected after moving authenticator to a new phone
tickets.description: Customer migrated their authenticator app to a new phone from a backup. The entry for our app shows codes, but none are accepted.
tickets.resolution_notes: The backup restored an entry from an earlier enrollment that had since been replaced, so its secret no longer matched the account. After the customer's admin verified the user's identity, we reset 2FA for that single user and they enrolled again from the new phone. Sign-in with the new code succeeded.

tickets.subject: 2FA code accepted on website but refused in mobile app
tickets.description: Same user, same authenticator: pasting the code works on the website, but the mobile app answers 'Code must be 6 digits'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The authenticator copies codes with a space in the middle ('123 456'), and the mobile app's input validation counted the space instead of stripping it. The user typed the digits manually as an immediate workaround, and a mobile app update now removes whitespace before validating. Confirmed the user signed in with a pasted code on the updated app.

tickets.subject: First code after scanning QR is 'invalid' during enrollment
tickets.description: A new user scanning the 2FA setup QR code gets 'Invalid code' when confirming enrollment. They had left the setup page open while hunting for their phone.
tickets.resolution_notes: The enrollment secret expires after ten minutes, and the page had quietly generated a new QR code on refresh, so the scanned secret was out of date. The user deleted the old entry, scanned the current code and confirmed enrollment successfully. The setup page now shows a countdown and warns when the code is replaced.

tickets.subject: Users stuck in 2FA enrollment loop after enforcement
tickets.description: Since the admin turned on 'Require two-factor authentication', some users finish enrolling, sign in, and are asked to enroll all over again. It seems to hit people who started on their phones.
tickets.resolution_notes: Users who began enrollment in the mobile app and finished in the browser had the enrollment saved against a temporary session that was discarded at sign-in. Changed the flow to store enrollment on the account immediately and cleared the incomplete enrollment state for the affected users. All 14 users enrolled once and were not prompted again.

tickets.classification_rationale: Touches who may perform the reset, but the request is recovering a user's second factor so they can sign in, so auth rather than perm.
tickets.subject: Admin cannot find option to reset a user's 2FA
tickets.description: A user lost their phone and has no recovery codes. The admin who handles access requests opened the user's profile but sees no way to reset two-factor authentication.
tickets.resolution_notes: Resetting another user's second factor is limited to workspace owners, and the requesting admin held the editor-admin role. The workspace owner verified the user's identity through the customer's helpdesk process and reset 2FA for that one account. The user enrolled a new device and signed in.

tickets.subject: Printed recovery code not accepted
tickets.description: User is typing a recovery code from a printed sheet saved two years ago, and the login page says it is invalid.
tickets.resolution_notes: Codes generated in the older format mixed the digit zero and the capital letter O, and the user had typed the wrong one. After verifying the user, we pointed out the ambiguous character and they signed in with the code. They then generated a fresh set of recovery codes, which now use an alphabet without look-alike characters.

tickets.subject: 'Trust this device' ignored, 2FA asked every morning
tickets.description: Users at a grocery chain tick 'Trust this device for 30 days' but still get a code prompt every single morning.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's managed browser policy deletes all cookies when the browser closes, which removed the device-trust cookie each evening. The customer's IT team added the app domain to the policy's list of sites allowed to keep cookies. Users were not prompted on the following two mornings.

tickets.subject: Some users never prompted after 2FA became mandatory
tickets.description: The admin made 2FA mandatory a week ago, but the enrollment report still lists 17 users without a second factor, and those users say they were never asked.
tickets.resolution_notes: Enforcement took effect at each user's next sign-in, and those users still had long-lived sessions from before the change. After notifying staff, the admin used 'Sign out all sessions' so everyone re-authenticated, and enforcement now also ends existing password-only sessions within 24 hours. All 17 users had enrolled within two days.

tickets.subject: Reporting login locked every night around 02:00
tickets.description: The customer's reporting login is found locked each morning. The audit log shows a burst of failed password attempts at about 02:00 from 192.0.2.40.
tickets.resolution_notes: A scheduled script on the customer's reporting server still signed in with the password that had been rotated the week before, and each run tripped the lockout threshold. The customer moved the script to an API key held in their secrets manager instead of a password. No lockouts occurred over the following week.

tickets.subject: Analyst locked out every Monday before starting work
tickets.description: Finance analyst reports finding their account locked every Monday morning, although they haven't typed their password since Friday.
tickets.resolution_notes: A shared reporting PC ran an old version of the spreadsheet add-in that stored the analyst's previous password, and its weekend refresh kept retrying until the lockout policy triggered. Upgraded the add-in on that PC, which uses a personal token instead of a stored password, and had the analyst sign in again. The following Monday the account was not locked.

tickets.subject: Repeated lockout notices for a regional admin
tickets.description: The customer keeps receiving lockout notices for one regional admin. Failed logins in the audit log come from 203.0.113.45, which the customer traced to a back-office PC in one of their stores.
tickets.resolution_notes: That PC's browser autofilled the admin's outdated password and reloaded the sign-in page on a timer. The store team removed the saved credentials, and the screen now shows the store dashboard through a read-only TV display link instead of the admin's account. Lockout notices stopped the same day.

tickets.subject: Lockout lasts far longer than 30 minutes
tickets.description: User was told lockouts clear after 30 minutes but has now been locked out for more than two hours.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each sign-in attempt made during the lockout restarted the 30-minute timer, and the user had kept trying every so often. Unlocked the account after identity verification and changed the lockout page to show the remaining time and warn that further attempts extend it. The user signed in successfully.

tickets.subject: User still locked out after admin unlock
tickets.description: The customer's admin unlocked a user on the users page, but the user still sees 'Your account is locked' when signing in through SSO.
tickets.resolution_notes: The message came from the customer's identity provider, which had its own lockout after failed password attempts; the workspace lock had already been cleared. The customer's IdP administrator unlocked the directory account. The user signed in through SSO immediately afterwards.

tickets.subject: Opening a second workspace signs me out of the first
tickets.description: A consultant who supports two retail brands is signed out of brand A's workspace whenever they open brand B's in another tab.
tickets.resolution_notes: The session cookie was shared across workspaces, so signing in to the second workspace replaced the first session. As a workaround the consultant uses a separate browser profile per workspace; support for concurrent per-workspace sessions was tracked for a later release. The consultant confirmed both workspaces stayed signed in with separate profiles.

tickets.subject: Switching tabs between client workspaces forces re-login
tickets.description: An agency analyst who manages three clients' workspaces keeps landing on the sign-in page when moving between tabs, and is tired of juggling separate browser profiles.
tickets.resolution_notes: All workspaces shared a single session cookie, so each new sign-in displaced the previous one. This release scopes sessions per workspace so several can be active in one browser. After the update the analyst kept three workspaces open in tabs for a full day without being signed out.

tickets.subject: Signed out after 12 hours even while working
tickets.description: Users on long store-opening shifts are forced to sign in again partway through the day, sometimes in the middle of a task.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace policy sets a 12-hour absolute session lifetime that applies regardless of activity, unlike the idle timeout users expected. The admin chose to keep the limit for security reasons, so we added a warning banner ten minutes before expiry so users can save their work. Users confirmed seeing the banner before the next forced sign-in.

tickets.classification_rationale: Looks like a display problem, but the screen shows the sign-in page because the session expired, so auth rather than render.
tickets.subject: Store office TV shows the sign-in page every morning
tickets.description: A sales dashboard left running on a TV in a store office is back on the sign-in page each morning. It was signed in with a manager's account the evening before.
tickets.resolution_notes: The dashboard's automatic refresh did not count as user activity, so the manager's session hit the idle timeout overnight. The admin created a TV display link, a read-only and revocable link meant for unattended screens, and opened it on the TV instead of a personal session. The display stayed live through the next three days.

tickets.subject: Session ends right after successful login
tickets.description: One user signs in, sees the dashboard for a split second, and is returned to the login page. Other users on the same network have no problem.
tickets.resolution_notes: The user's laptop clock was set a day ahead, so the browser treated the session cookie's expiry date as already past. The user corrected the clock, and we changed the session cookie to a relative max-age so client clock errors can no longer expire it early. The user stayed signed in normally.

tickets.subject: 'Remember me' does nothing on store PCs
tickets.description: Store staff tick 'Remember me' but must sign in again every time the browser is reopened.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace has 'Allow persistent sessions' turned off, which overrides the 'Remember me' option; the admin confirmed this is intentional for shared store computers. We now hide the checkbox when the policy disables it so staff are not misled. The admin verified the checkbox no longer appears on the store PCs.

tickets.classification_rationale: The dashboard renders correctly once a session exists; the loop comes from the blocked session cookie, so auth rather than render.
tickets.subject: Embedded dashboard in intranet keeps asking to sign in
tickets.description: Customer embedded a dashboard on their intranet homepage. Users see our login form inside the frame; after signing in it reloads and asks again.
tickets.resolution_notes: The browser blocks cookies set inside a cross-site iframe, so the session created in the frame was discarded on every reload. Workaround: the intranet tile now opens the dashboard in a new tab, where the session persists; token-based embedding for framed dashboards was tracked for a later release. Users confirmed the new-tab link kept them signed in.

tickets.subject: Staff portal frame returns to sign-in on every page view
tickets.description: Store managers open the weekly sales dashboard inside the customer's staff portal (portal.example.net). Signing in within the frame appears to work, then the frame reloads to the sign-in form.
tickets.resolution_notes: Session cookies set within the cross-site frame were being dropped by the browser. Enabled signed embed links, released this quarter, which hand the frame a short-lived embed token instead of relying on a cookie. Store managers reloaded the framed dashboard repeatedly without any sign-in prompt.

tickets.subject: Embedded view fine in Chrome, sign-in loop in Safari
tickets.description: The customer's embedded store dashboard works for staff on Chrome but loops back to the login form for anyone using Safari, including all iPads.
tickets.resolution_notes: Safari blocks third-party cookies by default, so the framed session was never stored there, while the customer's Chrome configuration still accepted them. Moved the customer's embed to signed embed links, which do not depend on cookies inside the frame. iPad and Safari users loaded the embedded dashboard without a loop.

tickets.subject: Login loop only on the custom analytics domain
tickets.description: Customer serves the app at analytics.retail.example.com. Users sign in, briefly see the home page and are sent back to sign-in; the default app address works.
tickets.resolution_notes: Another internal application on the customer's parent domain set a cookie named 'session' for all of .retail.example.com, which collided with our session cookie on the custom domain. Renamed our cookie with a host-only prefix so parent-domain cookies cannot overwrite it. Sign-in on the custom domain worked for every tested user.

tickets.subject: 'Session expired, please try again' on the login form
tickets.description: One user always gets 'Session expired, please try again' when submitting the login form, however quickly they type. It started after they installed a privacy browser extension.
tickets.resolution_notes: The extension blocked session storage on our domain, so the login form's anti-forgery value was missing on submit. As an immediate step the user allowed site storage for our domain in the extension; we then added a cookie-based fallback so the form works even when storage is blocked. Verified sign-in with the extension in its default mode after the release.

tickets.classification_rationale: An allow list is involved, but it governs browser cookie storage for sign-in rather than network reachability, so auth rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: 'Your browser blocked a required cookie' on managed laptops
tickets.description: On the customer's managed laptops the login page shows 'Your browser blocked a required cookie'. Staff signing in from personal devices are not affected.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's browser policy allows cookies only for listed sites, and the list still named our previous app domain from before the domain move. Their IT team added the current app domain to the policy's cookie allow list. Once the policy refreshed, users on managed laptops signed in normally.

tickets.subject: Invitation links expired before new hires used them
tickets.description: The customer's admin invited new store staff on a Friday; on Monday every link showed 'This invitation has expired'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Invitations were valid for 48 hours, which a weekend easily exceeds. The admin resent the invitations, and we extended invitation validity to seven days, with expired links now offering a 'Request a new invite' button. All the new staff activated their accounts from the resent links.

tickets.classification_rationale: Resembles a missing-permission case, but the user had signed in under the wrong identity, so auth rather than perm.
tickets.subject: New user sees no workspace after accepting invite
tickets.description: A newly hired buyer accepted their invitation and signed in, but the app says 'You don't belong to any workspace yet'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The buyer had chosen 'Sign up' with a different alias address instead of accepting while signed in as the invited address, creating a separate account unconnected to the invitation. Removed the stray account at the customer's request and resent the invitation, which the buyer accepted with the invited address. They now see the workspace and its dashboards.

tickets.subject: Invitations show 'already accepted' though nobody accepted
tickets.description: New staff at a garden centre chain open their invitation email and see 'This invitation was already accepted', yet they cannot sign in and have never set a password.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's mail security service opens links in inbound mail, and invitation acceptance was triggered by that request, leaving half-activated accounts with no password. Applied the confirm-before-redeem step already used for password reset links to invitation acceptance, and reset the affected accounts. All six new staff members activated their accounts from fresh invitations.

tickets.subject: Bulk invite: 9 of 60 staff never got an invitation
tickets.description: Admin bulk-invited 60 store employees from a CSV file. Nine say no invitation ever arrived, and the user list shows them as 'Invite failed'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Those rows had trailing spaces after the email address, which made the addresses invalid and the invitations undeliverable. Changed the bulk import to trim whitespace and flag invalid rows before sending, then resent the nine invitations. All nine employees activated their accounts the same afternoon.

tickets.subject: Invite link says it belongs to a different workspace
tickets.description: An external consultant who already uses the product for another client gets 'This invitation belongs to a different workspace' when clicking a new invitation.
tickets.resolution_notes: The consultant's browser was signed in to their other client's workspace, and the accept flow compared the invitation with the active session's workspace instead of the invited email address. The accept page now asks the user to confirm or switch accounts before accepting. The consultant accepted the invitation and can switch between both workspaces.

tickets.classification_rationale: Users saw no dashboards, but the cause was identity matching at sign-in rather than role assignment, so auth rather than perm.
tickets.subject: SSO users land in new, empty accounts after email format change
tickets.description: After the customer's IT team changed staff email addresses from first.last to first initial plus surname, users signing in via SSO see an empty home page and the product tour.
tickets.resolution_notes: SSO matched users by email address, so the new addresses created brand-new accounts through just-in-time provisioning instead of reaching the existing ones. We moved the existing accounts to the new addresses, removed the empty duplicates, and switched this workspace's SSO matching to the identity provider's immutable user ID. Saved dashboards and views reappeared for users at their next sign-in.

tickets.subject: Buyer's saved views gone after company domain migration
tickets.description: A buyer at a homeware retailer says that since the company moved to a new email domain, signing in shows the welcome tour and none of their saved views or subscriptions.
tickets.resolution_notes: The identity provider now sends the buyer's new address, which did not match the login email on their existing account, so a second account was created at sign-in. Merged them by moving the new login email onto the original account and deleting the empty one. The buyer's saved views were back at their next sign-in.

tickets.subject: SSO says email already in use in another workspace
tickets.description: Following a rebrand, one of the customer's planners gets 'An account with this email already exists in another workspace' when signing in through SSO.
tickets.resolution_notes: The identity provider began sending the planner's new address, which did not match their existing login, and that address had once been used for a personal trial workspace. With the planner's approval we closed the old trial and set the new address as the login email on their existing account. SSO sign-in then went straight to the customer's workspace.

tickets.subject: Mobile app says 'User not found' for some accounts
tickets.description: A handful of users can sign in on the web, but the mobile app tells them 'User not found'. Every one of their login emails contains capital letters.
tickets.resolution_notes: Those accounts came from an old import that kept the original capitalization, and the mobile sign-in endpoint compared emails case-sensitively. Normalized stored login emails to lowercase and made the lookup case-insensitive. The affected users signed in on mobile successfully.

tickets.classification_rationale: Includes a DNS verification step, but the problem is which email domains SSO sign-in recognizes, so auth rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: Password login works but SSO says 'No account found'
tickets.description: Employees of the customer's subsidiary (retail-group.example.com) cannot use SSO, although the parent company's domain works and the same employees can still sign in with a password.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace SSO configuration listed only the parent company's verified domain, so SSO lookups for the subsidiary domain found no workspace. The admin verified the subsidiary domain with the DNS TXT check and added it to the SSO configuration. Subsidiary employees signed in through SSO the same day.

tickets.classification_rationale: The token identifies an individual user in the add-in rather than a system integration, so auth rather than api.
tickets.subject: Spreadsheet add-in fails after password reset
tickets.description: A pricing analyst reset their password on Tuesday, and since then the spreadsheet add-in returns 'Token revoked' whenever it refreshes data.
tickets.resolution_notes: Resetting a password revokes all of the user's personal access tokens by design, and the add-in still held the old token. The analyst signed out of the add-in and authorized it again, after which it refreshed data normally. We also updated the reset confirmation email to say that connected tools must be re-authorized.

tickets.classification_rationale: This is a personal token authenticating one person, not an integration key, so auth rather than api.
tickets.subject: Command-line report tool rejects credentials after password change
tickets.description: An analyst who pulls weekly figures with our command-line tool says it began failing with 'invalid credentials' on the day they changed their password. Their scripts are untouched.
tickets.resolution_notes: The tool authenticates with the analyst's personal token, and changing the password revoked every personal token on the account as designed. The analyst generated a new personal token and updated the tool's configuration file. The next scheduled run downloaded the figures successfully.

tickets.subject: Personal tokens stop working after 90 days
tickets.description: Users of the spreadsheet add-in are surprised to find it asking for authorization again roughly every three months.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace security policy sets a 90-day maximum lifetime for personal tokens, and nothing warned users before expiry. Added a reminder email seven days before a token expires and a clear 'token expired' message in the add-in; the admin kept the 90-day limit. Users received the reminder before the next expiry and re-authorized without opening a support request.

tickets.subject: Add-in sign-in window closes immediately
tickets.description: Clicking 'Sign in' in the desktop spreadsheet add-in opens a small window that closes straight away. No error appears and the add-in stays signed out. The customer uses SSO.
tickets.resolution_notes: The add-in host blocked the pop-up that the SSO redirect needed, closing it before the identity provider page loaded. Workaround: the user signed in with the add-in's device-code option, which completes sign-in in a normal browser; a permanent fix that opens SSO in a supported dialog is planned for the next add-in version. The user was signed in and refreshing data the same day.

tickets.subject: Personal token rejected in second workspace
tickets.description: An analyst's token works in the add-in for the head-office workspace but is refused with 'Unauthorized workspace' when pointed at the outlet-stores workspace.
tickets.resolution_notes: Personal tokens are scoped to the workspace where they are created, and this one was generated in head office. The analyst generated a second token from inside the outlet-stores workspace. Both workbooks refreshed with their respective tokens.

tickets.subject: Fingerprint unlock stopped working after phone update
tickets.description: Since updating their phone's operating system, a district manager is asked for a password every time they open the mobile app, and the fingerprint option has disappeared.
tickets.resolution_notes: The OS update invalidated the device key that protected the stored credential for biometric unlock, and the app did not offer to set it up again. Released an app update that re-prompts biometric setup after one password sign-in when the key is invalid. After updating, the manager re-enabled fingerprint unlock and it worked on the next launch.

tickets.subject: Mobile SSO stuck on a 'Redirecting…' page
tickets.description: When store managers sign in with SSO in the mobile app, the identity provider page accepts their credentials and then sits on 'Redirecting…' without ever returning to the app.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's device management profile stops the browser from opening custom URL schemes, so the hand-back to the app never happened. Switched the app's SSO return to a verified https app link, which the profile permits. Store managers completed SSO sign-in and returned to the app normally.

tickets.classification_rationale: Caused by a workspace rename, but the impact is that users cannot sign in, so auth rather than workspace_admin.
tickets.subject: Mobile app says workspace not found after rename
tickets.description: Store staff typing their workspace name on the mobile app's sign-in screen get 'Workspace not found' ever since the workspace was renamed last week.
tickets.resolution_notes: The app looked the workspace up by the old identifier it had cached at first sign-in, which the rename retired. Cleared the cached value through a server-side flag, and the app now finds the workspace from the user's email domain. Staff signed in after restarting the app.

tickets.subject: Android app signs users out whenever it is backgrounded
tickets.description: On some Android phones the app demands a fresh sign-in every time users switch away and come back. iPhone users at the same customer stay signed in for days.
tickets.resolution_notes: The app saved its refreshed session token only on a clean exit, and aggressive battery management on those devices killed the app before that happened. An app update now writes the token as soon as it is refreshed. Affected users stayed signed in after repeatedly backgrounding the updated app.

tickets.subject: Shared store tablet signs next user into previous account
tickets.description: On a shared store tablet, after one manager signs out, the next person taps 'Sign in with SSO' and lands straight in the previous manager's account without entering any credentials.
tickets.resolution_notes: Signing out ended the app session but left the identity provider session alive in the in-app browser, so the next SSO attempt silently reused it. The app now uses an ephemeral browser session for SSO and calls the identity provider's logout endpoint on sign-out. The customer tested two consecutive managers on the same tablet and each had to authenticate separately.

tickets.subject: New password rejected with no explanation
tickets.description: User choosing a new password gets 'Password does not meet requirements', but the form never says which requirement.
tickets.resolution_notes: The workspace policy requires at least one symbol, and the error message did not list unmet rules. Updated the form to show each requirement with a live check mark. The user set a compliant password on the next try.

tickets.subject: Self-made password flagged as breached
tickets.description: A customer's user insists their new password is unique, yet the form rejects it with 'This password has appeared in a data breach'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Breach screening compares new passwords with a list of known exposed passwords, and the user's choice was a common keyboard pattern with a year appended, which is on that list. Explained the check and suggested a passphrase generated by their password manager. The new passphrase was accepted.

tickets.subject: Forced password change keeps coming back
tickets.description: When the 90-day expiry prompt appears, the user changes their password successfully, signs in, and is immediately told the password has expired again.
tickets.resolution_notes: For accounts with a pending email-change verification, the password change saved the new hash but skipped updating the 'last changed' date, so the expiry check kept firing. Fixed the update so the date is always recorded and corrected it for the five affected accounts. The user signed in without another expiry prompt.

tickets.subject: Password with accented letter fails at login after reset
tickets.description: User set a new password containing 'é' through the reset page on their Mac. The reset reported success, but the login page rejects the very same password.
tickets.resolution_notes: The reset page and the login page normalized Unicode differently, so the accented character was stored in one form and submitted in another. Both pages now apply the same normalization before hashing and comparison. The user reset once more and signed in with the accented password.

tickets.subject: Stricter password rule not applied to existing users
tickets.description: Admin raised the minimum password length to 14 characters, yet staff with shorter passwords keep signing in without being asked to change them.
tickets.resolution_notes: New policy rules apply when a password is next set, not to existing passwords, by design. The admin used 'Require password change at next sign-in' for all password-based users, and the policy page now explains this behaviour. Within a week the policy report showed every password user compliant.
